episode_title: TDI Podcast: Where It All Started (#1000)

real_qa.q: What was Adam Curry's role in the early history of podcasting and the MTV industry?
real_qa.r: Adam Curry was at the beginning of podcasting as the pod father and helped create the medium. He also worked at MTV, arriving in late 1986 or 1987, during a time when venues like CBGB were still operating. He built incredible business around podcasting and did not sit back and watch the industry evolve, but evolved with it and changed with all the things he did.
real_qa.requete: Adam Curry pod father MTV podcasting history

real_qa.q: Why did Andrew Horowitz start The Disciplined Investor Podcast in 2007?
real_qa.r: Horowitz started the podcast in March 2007 after his publisher suggested he create a podcast to help market his book 'The Disciplined Investor: Essential Strategies for Success.' At the time, Horowitz did not know what a podcast was, and most people were unfamiliar with the medium. The idea was to create a show that went beyond headlines and talked honestly about markets, investing, the economy, and mistakes, while challenging the popular narrative.

real_qa.q: How many episodes and guests has The Disciplined Investor Podcast reached by its 1,000th episode?
real_qa.r: By episode 1,000, The Disciplined Investor Podcast has had more than 700 guests and has become one of the longest independent financial podcasts of all time. The podcast reached this milestone 20 years after starting in March 2007.

real_qa.q: What major market events and economic cycles did The Disciplined Investor Podcast cover over its 20-year run?
real_qa.r: Over 20 years, The Disciplined Investor discussed the financial crisis, the longest bull market in history, the pandemic collapse, zero interest rate policy (ZERP), stimulus checks, inflation cycles, rate hikes and drops, trade wars, technology booms, the AI boom, bubbles, crashes, and once-in-a-lifetime events like GameStop and meme stocks. Throughout these periods, many experts on the show explained why the old rules no longer applied, only for the old rules to come back and prove relevant.
real_qa.requete: Disciplined Investor Podcast market events 20 years coverage

real_qa.q: What was Interactive Brokers' average annual return for individual clients over three years according to the episode?
real_qa.r: Interactive Brokers' individual clients averaged a 24.3% annual return over the past three years, beating the S&P 500. The broker offers lower costs, competitive rates, and access to more than 170 global markets to help investors keep more of what they earn.

guest.bio_context: Adam Curry was an early pioneer in podcasting known as 'the pod father' who helped create the medium itself and built incredible business around it. He worked at MTV in the late 1980s and early 1990s, and has been a long-time friend and inspiration to Andrew Horowitz, helping influence Horowitz's approach to podcasting and sound quality.
